overview.heading: How the Event Flyer Maker works
paragraphs: Enter the event name, the date and time, and the venue. Add a tagline, up to four highlights and a call to action if you want them, and pick one of ten styles. PiCraft designs a complete portrait flyer with a clear hierarchy: the event name largest, then the date and venue, then the details.
Everything on the flyer comes from what you typed. The design does not invent extra text, so the only wording on it is yours.
From one design you get a US Letter print file with bleed, a 1080×1350 px image for Instagram and Facebook feeds, and a 1080×1920 px version for stories.

whatYouGet.title: Letter print PDF with bleed
whatYouGet.description: An 8.5×11 inch flyer with 0.125 inch bleed at 300 DPI, to print at a shop or at the office.

whatYouGet.title: A print JPG
whatYouGet.description: The same print file as a JPG for services that prefer images.

whatYouGet.title: Instagram and Facebook image
whatYouGet.description: A 1080×1350 px 4:5 portrait, the shape that takes up the most room in the feed.

whatYouGet.title: A Stories version
whatYouGet.description: A 1080×1920 px 9:16 image, with the flyer centered on a soft blurred background.

whatYouGet.title: Ten styles
whatYouGet.description: Community, neon nightlife, gig poster, professional, gala, festival and more.

useCases.title: Community events
useCases.description: Markets, fundraisers, school fairs and neighborhood meetups, printed for noticeboards and posted online.

useCases.title: Music and nightlife
useCases.description: Gigs, club nights and open mics, with a poster look and a feed-sized version.

useCases.title: Small business promotions
useCases.description: Grand openings, sales and workshops, with a call to action pointing to your website.

useCases.title: Corporate and professional events
useCases.description: Meetups, webinars and conferences, with a clean professional style.

useCases.title: Charity and club events
useCases.description: Sports days, bake sales and charity runs, with the highlights listed clearly.

useCases.title: Holiday gatherings
useCases.description: Neighborhood potlucks, Halloween parties and holiday open houses fit the flyer, which carries the date, time and venue you type. For a friendly picture to post beside it, a [Halloween costume portrait](/create/photo-trend-maker/halloween-portrait) or a [Christmas card portrait](/create/photo-trend-maker/christmas-card) made from your own photo works as a companion image, while the flyer stays the source for the details.

tips.title: Lead with a short event name
tips.description: The name is the largest text on the flyer. Two to five words read best from a distance.

tips.title: Put the date and time together
tips.description: "Friday, July 18 · 6–11 PM" in one line keeps the key facts in one place.

tips.title: Limit the highlights to four short lines
tips.description: "Free entry", "30+ food vendors" and "Live DJ" read at a glance. Long lines are hard to read.

tips.title: Use one clear call to action
tips.description: A website or phone number is enough. Don't add several ways to reply.

tips.title: Match the style to the crowd
tips.description: Gala and professional suit formal events, neon and festival suit a younger crowd, community suits families.

tips.title: Check readability from a distance
tips.description: Hold the printed flyer at arm's length or view it at thumbnail size. The event name and date should still be clear.

tips.title: Use the right version in the right place
tips.description: Use the Letter file for printing, the 4:5 image for the feed and the story version for stories.

styleGuide.heading: Choosing a flyer style
styleGuide.intro: The style sets the colors, the lettering and the energy. Pick one that fits your audience.

items.title: Bright community
items.description: Cheerful colors and friendly shapes. Fits markets, fairs and family events.

items.title: Neon nightlife
items.description: Dark backgrounds with glowing color. Fits clubs, parties and late events.

items.title: Gig poster
items.description: A bold, printed-poster look. Fits concerts, open mics and bands.

items.title: Clean professional
items.description: A restrained layout with clear type. Fits business events and talks.

items.title: Elegant gala
items.description: Refined type and rich accents. Fits fundraisers, dinners and awards.

items.title: Music festival
items.description: Colorful and energetic. Fits outdoor festivals and multi-act events.

items.title: Vintage retro
items.description: A nostalgic palette and type. Fits themed nights and anniversaries.

items.title: Sports & fitness
items.description: Dynamic shapes and strong color. Fits races, classes and tournaments.

items.title: Warm charity
items.description: Friendly and welcoming. Fits bake sales, drives and charity events.

items.title: Tech & startup
items.description: Modern gradients and clean type. Fits hackathons, meetups and launches.

checklist.heading: Before you print or post
items: Check the event name, date, time and venue against your plans.
Confirm the website or phone number in the call to action works.
Print one test copy and read it from a distance before printing a batch.
Choose the right file: the Letter PDF for printing, the 4:5 image for the feed, the story image for stories.
If you print at home, expect a thin white margin because most home printers cannot print to the edge.
If you print at a shop, upload the PDF with bleed and ask the shop to trim to Letter size.
Post the digital version a few weeks ahead and again a few days before the event.

limits: The Letter size is fixed. For A4, ask your printer to scale it or re-create the design in an editor.
It does not add a QR code or a logo. Put your website in the call to action, or add those in an image editor.
The print file is upscaled from the generated design, so bold and simple layouts print sharpest.
The text is part of the image, so changing a word means generating again.
Long highlights and small print can be hard to read. Keep the text short.
